evidence.claim: Cardholder C11923 denies the flagged $131.30 charge 3583368 of 2016-12-29 and also denies the two earlier identical $131.30 charges 3193355 and 3565743, stating there is no subscription or instalment plan at that amount and that they do not own or have access to a Samsung SM-G610F phone.

Flagged txn 3583368 was made online from 'SM-G610F Build/NRD90M | unknown | chrome 66.0 for android | unknown' with device_new_flag 'New' and new_device_for_card true \u2014 a device with no history on card C11923-K2.
The $131.30 amount is 3.33x the 180-day card mean of $39.45 (amount_z 2.55) though below the card max of $486.52; the card's history is 100% online product C.
The apparent recurring pattern is not monthly: only 2 prior same-amount txns, 123 days apart (2016-08 and 2016-12), looks_monthly false, and the cardholder denies both, so R7 does not apply.

Memory of structurally linked cases is dominated by confirmed fraud of exactly this type (94 card_not_present_new_device, 64 card_not_present_fraud vs 6 cleared), including CC-5499 and CC-5417 where one to three unrecognised online charges of comparable size were confirmed fraudulent and the card blocked.

Policy R2 directs BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE when the customer denies the transaction; FILE_REPORT is not triggered here as denied exposure is $393.90 and the flagged device is not among the rare shared device profiles.

case.summary: Cardholder C11923 disputed a $131.30 online charge (3583368, 2016-12-29 03:27) on card C11923-K2. The charge came from a Samsung SM-G610F device flagged New for this account, at 3.33x the card's mean amount. On validation the cardholder denied not only this charge but also the two earlier identical $131.30 charges (3193355, 3565743), and denied owning the device, removing the possibility that this was their own irregular recurring charge. Denial plus a new-device card-not-present charge plus a strongly fraud-weighted memory base makes this card-not-present fraud from a new device. Total denied exposure is $393.90, below the reporting threshold, and the flagged device is not a rare profile shared with other cards, so a case and a block are warranted rather than a regulatory filing.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: The cardholder states they do not recognise the two earlier $131.30 charges (3193355 in August and 3565743 in December) and has no subscription or instalment plan at that amount, and they deny making any purchase in the early hours of 29 December 2016; they do not own or have access to a Samsung SM-G610F Android phone. They request the card be blocked and all three charges disputed.

next_best_actions.what_changed: The customer validation reply denied all three $131.30 charges and denied any access to the SM-G610F device, ruling out the recurring-legitimate-charge explanation and moving the assessment from uncertain (0.45) to fraud (0.84).

sar.reason: Case only, no report: fraud with exposure $131.30 <= $1,000, no shared device/region link and a documented pattern, so no §3a condition holds.

stop_reason: Verification settled the question: customer_validation -> denies (policy §6). Verification response settles the question: the cardholder denies the charges, and with the new-device and amount-anomaly signals the case is above 0.85-adjacent certainty on at least three independent pieces of evidence; further requests would not change the decision.
